rv.q: No one could accuse All New People of excessive profundity, but it combines the comic and the poignant with undoubted panache.
But what promises to be a savagely black comedy turns into a muddled, meandering affair that reeks of self-gratification.
A shorter run of this show would reduce human suffering.

cn.t: Critics split on Braff's dark comedy, with some finding it a smart, sharp pleasure that never outstays its welcome, while others feel it fails to deliver on its promise of savage black humor.
